text: On Margaret Gilbert's joint commitment account of group belief, a group believes that p when:
choices: a strict majority of the group's members each individually believe that p.
every member of the group believes that p and each knows that the others believe it too.
its members are jointly committed to believe that p as a body, whether or not any individual member privately believes p.
the belief that p can be reached by majority voting on each premise even where this conflicts with majority voting on the conclusion.
explanation: Gilbert's non-summativism treats group belief as a performative joint commitment to uphold p 'as a body'; this can hold even when no member privately believes p, which is why it is not reducible to members' individual beliefs. Options 0 and 1 are summative (majority and unanimity) readings; option 3 describes the List and Pettit discursive dilemma, a distinct point about aggregation procedures. Only option 2 states Gilbert's account.
